I got credits to roll on my first run. As that is pretty much the end of what exists in the game's current state, there is very little motivation for me to continue playing and unlocking more upgrades and guns when i could already clear the game without them. The game itself isnt that bad but its just lacking content and depth that others in the genre are packed with. Its definitely worth checking out either in the future when more content has been added, or if you really think its for you and are willing to look past some of the drawbacks.

Wish I could return it. Just a spaz game. All you do it die because your health depletes within .5 seconds. I played for 2.4 hours and it just made me angry. If you focus on trying to get health (making buildings fall on enemies so when you kill them you get health) then you get mobbed and destroyed by them all. I despise when people glorify these games as "easy" or a "relaxed shooter" no. This is an insane shooter super overwhelming and you just die with minimal progression. I don't want to sink hours into a game to crawl an inch, even more so when it's this difficult. I doubt I will be ever playing this again. Want to get very angry at a game? Play this. Edit: I will play more, I realize I have a skill issue. I am terrible at FPS games so it's my own fault for attempting to find this enjoyable. It is fun but I am very very very bad at it. So personally I don't recommend it but for everyone else, YOU WILL LOVE IT!

先说结论，虚空破坏者可玩性高，耐玩性一般，优化一般，问题不少，总体来说属于特别好评。 肉鸽加fps注定下限高，但虚空破坏者有几个挺重要的缺点： 1.武器差距太大，只有步枪能玩，喷子手枪射手全是废物，我还以为会像塔那样有专属卡池，结果是共通的，这个问题太大了，让游戏寿命少了不止一半。 2.boss战设计，第一次打的时候还没意识到什么问题，后面发现，抓碎片太遮挡视野了，看不到boss动向。boss战没有小怪本意是为了简单点，但是中后期闭着眼都能过，到了boss那里必须要老老实实拆柱子，拆半天回一丝血，失误个一两下就完了，可以看出来是想模仿doom，也有点像mgs4里季风boss战，但是到了boss那里我只能像条狗一样跑来跑去扔垃圾，这点很不爽，太不爽了，就这一点让我都想差评了。希望能减少boss的攻击改为召唤小怪，并且改变出招方式，这样能够吸血续航，不至于boss和普通关的体验差距太大。 3.数值的可视化，有些模块是百分比加伤害，有些是固定增伤，但是不知道到底基础伤害是多少加了多少，如果背包里面有个数值表能够更好的规划一下。 4.基础设置，初始灵敏度设计的有些过于简陋了，我弄了好久才找到一个能用的设置，并且优化不怎么好，没有dlss之类的。 5.最后就是一些比较小的问题了，比如模组不够丰富，怪物不够丰富什么的，这些都是小问题，相信制作者以后会更新更多新东西的。 Conclusion first:​​ Void Breaker has high playability, average longevity, and decent optimization, but it has quite a few issues. Overall, it’s still a ​Very Positive​ experience. The Roguelike + FPS formula inherently has a high baseline, but Void Breaker suffers from several critical flaws: ​1.Huge weapon disparity (Rifles only, everything else is trash)​​ – Only rifles are viable; shotguns, pistols, and ranged weapons are all useless. I thought there would be exclusive card pools for different weapons like in Risk of Rain, but no—they’re all shared. This is a ​huge problem​ that cuts the game’s lifespan in half. ​2.Boss fight design​ – At first, I didn’t notice, but later on, I realized how bad it is. The "fragment grabbing" mechanic blocks too much of the screen, making it hard to see the boss’s movements. Boss fights intentionally lack minions to keep things simple, but by the mid-to-late game, they become brain-dead easy. Then, when you finally reach the boss, you’re forced to ​grind through tedious pillar-breaking​ just to recover a tiny bit of HP—mess up once or twice, and you’re dead. It tries to mimic DOOM and even resembles the Monsoon boss fight from MGS4, but instead of stylish combat, you’re just ​running around like a dog, throwing junk to survive. This is ​extremely frustrating, and it’s the main reason I almost gave this game a negative review. ​Please reduce boss damage, add summonable minions, and change their attack patterns​ so players can heal through damage sponging—otherwise, the boss fights feel way worse than regular levels. ​3.Lack of numerical clarity​ – Some modules give percentage-based damage bonuses, others give flat bonuses, but you have no idea what the base damage is or how much you’re actually gaining. A ​simple in-inventory damage calculator or breakdown​ would help with build planning. ​4.Basic settings & optimization​ – The initial sensitivity settings are way too basic—I spent ages just trying to find a usable configuration. Also, the optimization isn’t great; there’s no DLSS or similar tech. ​5.Minor issues​ – Things like limited mod variety and not enough enemy types are smaller problems, but I’m sure the devs will add more content in updates.

Poor game performance. Combat sucked. No radar/minimap. Enemies overpowered and hard to dodge. Always taking damage and running away while looking for objects to throw at them. Can only get health and ammo by throwing objects at them (with followup kill) + sometimes chests drop them. They separate Dash from Sprint, so you need to mess with a separate key to do Dashes while sprinting and jumping and sliding. I hated the combat. Gun doesn't do too much, same with grenades, so you have to try to spam the interact key while facing random directions until it pulls in some random object for you to throw to try to damage the enemies (who half the time dodge it), and hitting them with objects is the only way to stagger them (and the only way to get health or ammo drops is to kill staggered enemies). Enemies spam bullet grenades in 360 directions and spirals, inflicting enough damage to insta drop you to like 30% hp, which really sucks because there isn't even a radar or minimap to help detect them. So i spent the whole time running away, hiding behind obstacles while spamming for an object to grab to throw at them, taking tons of damage every time i looking one direction because things would sneak up from another direction. Then after each area, i had to spend time running around looking for random purple gem boxes to break because they are the only thing that gives you that currency to upgrade your character between runs. Once i finally got enough gems to upgrade to the assault rifle, i went into a run to try to use it and the recoil was like a shotgun or something, and it was absolutely unbearable (I couldn't keep the aim on the mob i was shooting), so i decided to call it for this game. If i can't enjoy any aspect of the combat then no thank you. Refunded game. Game also runs terribly. I wanted to try to improve it by reducing the resolution and upscaling, but they only had options for nvidia upscaling (I have an AMD GPU). The story, however, was pretty cool and reminded me of Portal, like the "cake is a lie" and "get out" escape from the system sort of deal. I liked the random location teleport areas that took you to a place off the map where you got to learn a little bit more about the background story while taking on mobs and learning the origin of how things led to the current situation.

This game was handcrafted by one guy with more passion than an entire Ubisoft conference. The intro slaps, the ambience is cinematic, and it runs smoother than my life choices on a 4-year-old PC. The sound design? Chef’s kiss. BUT. Why… just WHY do I lose all my weapon mods when I die? I just pulled a legendary, felt like John Wick in space and then boom, back to the stone age. Think Roboquest, but it hates you personally. You open loot boxes, get shiny toys, and then the game says: haha nope. Also that flying robot boss? Bro said “skill issue” and deleted me in 5 seconds. On Normal. No mercy, no checkpoints, just pain. [b]10/10 creativity, 2/10 emotional stability.[/b]

The game is sufficiently fun on anything below Insanity, Insanity and a lot of pretty questionable decisions make the game less than enjoyable, just a slog that overly penalises player for things beyond their control (such as map gen and enemies spawned in a chunk). The reliance on physics and crashing down entire buildings on enemies is fun, until the enemies get so tanky that they can and will survive three separate demolitions occuring right on their heads. Reliance on getting health and ammo from staggered enemies is fun, until there's no buidling left to crash and you have to rely on explosive boxes, which is fun until they run out (and on Insanity they will). Roguelike elements are fun, until you can't fish that one Grenade DMG amp for your life and without it you can't stagger minor enemies reliably with just one nade (without that you can't heal). Enemy variety is fun, until they blend into each other and you can only distinguish grunt from engineer because one can throw grenades and the other cannot. Elemental enemy variety is fun, until your entire screen is flooded with 8 letters of no fun allowed "IMMUNITY". You stacked volatile and freeze bombs? Too bad, now enjoy enemies that take no damage. And I can go on, but I suppose I won't, although a list won't hurt: tracking projectiles (droids and apex wolves), healing bots, camping sniper bots, enemies prefiring through walls, the worst sound design I've ever heard in a video game, you might as well turn it off (somehow this game is below R6: Siege in that regard, makes you think), cut to player's healing (Insanity problem), roguelike has too much junk, shooting builds almost no stagger, melee is borderline useless (unless you upgrade it fully, then it becomes marginally useful in first act), armored enemies and lack of vertical movement for the player (yes sling doesn't count, it's ♥♥♥♥). The game is fun, but not on Insanity. It turns into cookie cutter game, where you build same ♥♥♥♥ time and time over because nothing else works and that ain't fun.

游戏的主要模式是，先找（躲开海量的敌人的子弹）可投掷物品破坏有黄盾敌人的护盾（别看有投掷就以为像是死亡空间，这游戏能投掷的物品需要在地图上找），最好投掷没有浪费在没黄盾的敌人身上，然后（躲开海量的敌人的子弹）用投掷物和建筑破坏打敌人的失衡条，最后只需要（躲开海量的敌人的子弹）输出就行了，再然后会剩下只能被近战破盾的蓝盾敌人，拉扯一下（躲开敌人的子弹）最好一次面对一个然后近战破盾，非常简单。 这是你（在前两层）要躲开的子弹的类型的一部分：追踪的、大范围覆盖的、穿透掩体的、狙击的 这是你（在前两层）要对付的敌人的类型的一部分：自爆的、飞行的、瞬移的、零帧起手的、产小怪的、甚至有给其他敌人回血的 这是你能碰到的点的一部分：删核心模组给几个垃圾的、假如满血就是纯负面的、50%概率负面的、更别提一整局都买不起几个模组的商店。 这是最高稀有度的模组的一部分：必须一直跳否则扣血、需要调低FOV否则没效果、需要调低分辨率否则没效果、需要调高动态模糊否则没效果、需要调高鼠标灵敏度否则没效果。这些模组确实能增加伤害，但我宁愿把这些全删了多出紫色和金色模组。 地图。地图感觉很怪，敌人狙击你的时候到处都能打，敌人自爆炸你的时候到处都能来，你想找个地方躲的时候到处都是敌人。boss战的地图就更厉害了，就几个小岛，距离还远到必须用抓钩。 总结下来就是打的不爽，敌人又数量多又性能强，要打失衡才能回血，打失衡又要先破盾，盾又贼多，玩家局内成长很难凑出比较强的配装（说到底是不是根本就没几个很强的配装）。 还有亿些小问题，比如连接地图的可能会掉血的跳跃环节，折腾人又没啥意思；半自动没有按住连发，折腾人；去过的地点标记变色的逻辑很怪；按键显示地点的功能有时候会失效；容易忘记给研究留钱；第一个基地升级后的东西需要蹲下钻洞才能到；停止移动的时候枪支会发生奇怪的抽动（开始移动和移动中都没有）；敌人掉落的模块很小又没有标志容易错过（这个改了）；无限弹药的枪支长时间开火结束后枪械会大幅度回落；区域03 boss房打完之后捡战利品的地方会冻脚；

I really enjoy the core gameplay. However I loathe tradeoff upgrades in games. Things like: "+40% Damage but -80% accuracy," "More damage at close range but less damage at long range," or "More damage but slower rate of fire." This game is full of tradeoff upgrades and they just make the gunplay feel worse. If my accuracy starts going down too much then every shot becomes a dice roll. There are already plenty of optional difficulty modifiers so the dev shouldn't be afraid of making the game too easy because the player can scale the difficulty. For example: I made one of my runs full of elite and apex enemies on hard mode. Near the end of the run the room that got me was filled with a dozen armored ice elemental snipers that had a healing drone behind them. That enemy setup is already very difficult so I don't need two-steps-forward-one-step-back style gun upgrades. One could argue that I should just sell all these tradeoff upgrades and it would allow me to buy the upgrades I do enjoy. This is what I have been doing but selling mods doesn't yield very much shop currency and the shops have a limited selection. (Even more limited for me because I skip all of the sword upgrades but I'd say that is more a matter of personal preference.) There is the upgrade option for chests but that is quite expensive. I think the bigger issue is: Why do tradeoff upgrades even need to exist? Which aspect of making the gunplay worse for the player is supposed to be fun and exciting? It is not just upgrades either but also the bullet types (projectile mods) are tradeoffs too. From what I've seen every ammo type makes bullets travel slower and fall to the ground faster. There was a cool shuriken ammo type that I was excited for that could cause bleeding and ricochet to nearby enemies. I tested it out and the bullets took 5-7 business days just to reach the first enemy! Another ammo type is Mini Rockets. The description said it turns bullets into mini rockets but they are highly inaccurate. I didn't think it would be much of a problem since I was equipped with a shotgun at the time. Boy was I mistaken, the rockets couldn't even hit the broad side of a barn. No really, I tried shooting the wall of a building to see the spread but all three mini rockets made a 90 degree turn mid-flight and MISSED THE WALL! Now some might say "Why don't you just pickup the +100% bullet velocity upgrade before using the shuriken bullets or the accuracy upgrade before using the mini rockets?" But with the backpack slots being limited that means the tradeoff just to use these "upgrades" goes from low bullet velocity or high inaccuracy to less backpack space. I would be treating the symptoms but not the disease. What makes even less sense is that the ammo types are supposed to be limited quantity. So the core gameplay mechanic should already be a give and take system where the player has access to strong special ammo but will run out of the strong special ammo but will have to pickup more. Problem with that is the player gets hundreds of special ammo bullets that it is actually difficult to run out special ammo. So I think for that the dev should remove the ammo tradeoffs and adjust the carrying capacity of the ammo to be lower instead. In the end the gun modules were so bad that I used the default fast-cooldown infinite grenade as my main weapon instead to beat insane difficulty and chaos tier 20. So I'd consider it more of a first person "grenadier" instead of a first person "shooter" just kidding.

I am a huge fan of this game so far. The plot has me intrigued, the gameplay is very addicting, visually the game is beautiful (let's be real it's 2026 and any game on UE5 should) and in my opinion, VOID/BREAKER meshes a couple of different game elements together and the outcome is fantastic. Movement wise, game reminds me of Titanfall with the grappling, sliding and wall-running. All of this while being in a fast-paced procedurally generated environment that has buildings & objects with fairly impressive physics destruction. Having the ability to tether and throw objects adds a nice touch... Never played the entropy center but I did have that game on my radar for a good bit, and I will say, I enjoy seeing map parts and other elements of that game mixed in with this one. I also want to mention that the modifiers and abilities you are able to acquire and are pretty nifty, laying out the potential for dozens of different playstyles. Overall, I think this game is amazing in it's current EA state and I am absolutely thrilled to see what comes from the developer in the future!

This. Game. Slaps. It's still in early access but this is already a reeeally fun game. - DESTRUCTION PHYSICS - for f sake this should be in every game if possible. If you weren't around for Red Faction Guerilla when the servers were alive, I'm sorry. That sh was crazy. But this game gets really close to that level of complexity in destruction, and the scale and usefulness of it is sooo good. - AN ACTUALLY GOOD GRAPPLING HOOK - not the stupid kind where it just kind of pulls you to a point, one that rockets you across the world/stages with full physics simulation (which are big enough to take advantage of that) and even handles some sideways momentum (notes on that). Every game should have a gd grappling hook if it even remotely makes sense to. - Movement mechanics similar to Apex which are amazing. If you learn to time things right (if you're used to Apex you're gonna do just fine) you can absolutely rocket across the map and bamboozle enemies constantly. This game is bullet hell-ish, and if you get the fundamentals down you will dance through projectiles beautifully and feel like a... idk, like a ninja robot thing with digital superpowers. Stunning (and I don't use that word lightly) world design and effects, like, really impressive. - A story that actually has me asking questions (do take in the lore in this game, and look for the email terminals, it's worth it), and that is genuinely unique and completely cohesive and complementary to the entire design of the game. - And the ability to come up with some pretty crazy builds (though I have notes on that). Where it could get even better (and it's already kinda goated, glaze is owed): - This is a personal preference, but I think the dev is definitely borrowing from Apex in general, because it feels extremely similar. With that in mind, ADS should always have priority over sprint, and you should exit crouch when you jump unless you're using the toggle crouch keybind. Those would help flow and using your tools intuitively. Right now I feel like they kind of get in the way sometimes, in spite of being pretty clean. You learn to work with it, or I had to. Worth it though. -Crazier builds! I'm only 4 runs deep to be fair although I have finished... well I don't want to spoil that. But the point is I haven't really felt overpowered yet. There are a lot of really awesome abilities but I think they should snowball a little harder with each other, at least when you have a build with decent synergies. There are also some abilities which at this point I think are way stronger. - Grapple behavior: Right now too much angular momentum breaks the tether. I think a point I can rocket around more is needed. I want to be able to grab a hook and use it to do an entire 180 around it. I also think I should be able to generate angular momentum on it more. I keep wanting to so it like Pathfinders ability, and it's pretty close to that (again I think the dev was going for that) but not being able to force my self in a direction leads to too much running into structures. Please can I have tap strafing? Papa? Please? I keep instinctually trying to do it and I'm sad every time. Over all phenomenal game, it's already a 10/10 for me, and now I'm fiending for 11

One of the best roguelites I've ever played, made by a very talented solo dev. Even in current EA state, the game is highly replayable, with an engaging story and many elements that produce a satisfying roguelite experience. One of such elements is detailed dynamic destruction, allowing you to level entire structures on top of enemies. Level layouts are fully randomized, creating a different run each time. Gameplay is very smooth with no hitches the entire time on my setup. Future content is planned according to the dev's roadmap, meaning the game will only get better. Highly recommended even in its current EA state.
